key_insight: A single data-driven closure trained at the expected viscosity can be reused across stochastic realizations, with physical constraints improving ROM accuracy and robustness.
engineering_relevance: The approach can reduce the cost of uncertainty quantification for unsteady incompressible flows without training a separate closure for every viscosity realization.
method: Combine POD reduced-order modeling, spatial filtering, and stochastic collocation.
Reuse an expected-viscosity closure across random-viscosity realizations.
Impose physical constraints in CDDC-UQ-ROM to improve robustness.
evidence_signal: Tests on 2D cylinder flow with a 5D random viscosity field at mean Re = 100 and 500 found CDDC-UQ-ROM most accurate and robust for benchmark energy evolution across the cases considered.
watch_item: Reusing the expected-viscosity closure is an approximation; performance beyond the tested flow and viscosity settings remains to be established.
paper_title: Data-driven Correction Reduced-Order Stochastic Collocation Method for the Time-Dependent Navier-Stokes Equations
